chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Khaliji, from Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him)

about the opening Takbir, so he said: Seven. I said: It has been narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he used to say it once. He said: Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to say it once loudly and six times quietly.

key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةِ الِافْتِتَاحِ: The opening Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) at the start of prayer

ai.seo_question: How many times is the opening Takbir said in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the composition of the opening Takbir, distinguishing between the audible and silent repetitions to reconcile differing reports. This explanation highlights the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s complete practice, where the initial 'Allahu Akbar' is pronounced aloud to initiate the prayer, followed by six silent utterances, totaling seven. This detail underscores the precision in ritual jurisprudence (Fiqh) regarding the distinction between *Jahr* (audible) and *Ikhfat* (silent) recitations in Shia prayer. Additionally, the Prophet's consistent practice serves as a model for the Imams, reinforcing the continuity of divine guidance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-17 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Khalijee, on the authority of the father of Ali al-Hassan ibn Rashid, “I asked Al-Ridha (MGB)

about the number of times the Allahu Akbars (God is Great) are said before the start of the prayer. He (MGB) replied, ‘It is seven times.’ I said, ‘It has been narrated that God’s Prophet (MGB) said it only once.’ The Imam replied, ‘God’s Prophet (MGB) said it loudly once and said it quietly the other six times.’”
